newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PolyGram seeks to jejuvenate Motown.
newsitem.headline: PolyGram seeks to jejuvenate Motown.

text.p: Recorded music and film group PolyGram NV said a rejuvenation of its Motown label was a key objective of restructuring measures it announced on Wednesday.
"Management is taking positive steps to...make sure that the (Motown) label rejuvenates itself with new artists," PolyGram spokeswoman Amanda Conroy said.
"It has a fantastic back catalogue, obviously, but any record label needs to bring on new artists," she said.
PolyGram said it was making management changes at Motown and overhauling its artist and repertoire department, responsible for signing new talent, to revitalise the artist roster.
Motown's headquarters are also being moved to New York from Los Angeles. PolyGram acquired the black pop music label -- founded in Detroit by Berry Gordy -- in 1993.
Conroy said PolyGram was also taking action to offset the effects of several years of flat sales in the market for recordings of classical music.
"The way we're addressing this problem at PolyGram is to revamp our three classical labels -- Decca, Deutsche Grammophon, Philips Classics," she said.
"We've reinvigorated the management at PolyGram Classics and with their input we'll be changing the focus and direction and where necessary the organisation of our global classical music business."
PolyGram's entire music distribution and marketing operations in Europe would be reorganised with a view to making them more efficient in a difficult market, Conroy said.
Conroy said PolyGram could comment on its financial results for 1997 at this stage.
Philips Electronics NV has a 75 percent stake in PolyGram.
